summary:
We developed Lunar and Martian Unified Matching of Earth Analogs (L.U.M.E.A.), an interactive platform that helps identify places on Earth with conditions suitable for testing technologies and activities intended for future Moon and Mars missions. Users can select a planetary destination, a type of test, and a time of year to explore and compare potential Earth analog locations on a map.
L.U.M.E.A. considers factors such as temperature, lighting, terrain, and surface characteristics, presenting the results through clear suitability scores. It also explains which conditions are similar and where the comparison breaks down. The project makes the search for Earth analogs clearer, more organized, and accessible.
details:
Lunar and Martian Unified Matching of Earth Analogs (L.U.M.E.A.) is an interactive platform that helps to identify places on Earth where technologies and activities for future Moon and Mars missions could be tested.

The user selects a destination, a testing objective, and a month. The platform compares approximately 63,000 land regions using conditions such as temperature, sunlight, terrain, precipitation, wind, and estimated permafrost coverage. It combines these factors into suitability scores and displays potential locations on an interactive globe.

A location may be useful for navigating in low sunlight, for example, but less suitable for testing equipment in extreme cold. The user can explore known analog sites, adjust criteria, and see which conditions match.

As an additional feature, users can view satellite imagery of already confirmed Earth analog sites, sourced from scientific databases. These images provide visual references of established analog environments, helping users explore their geographical characteristics and better understand their relevance to lunar and Martian exploration.

The prototype uses NASA POWER, AWS Terrain Tiles, ESA CCI Permafrost, and NASA imagery. It was developed with Python, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Vite, and MapLibre GL JS.

Our team considered possible seasonal changes, missing data, uncertainty, and the fact that Earth cannot naturally reproduce conditions such as lunar gravity or the Martian atmosphere. L.U.M.E.A. is designed to help researchers narrow down potential testing locations.

Project Documentation: https://ascangel.github.io/repo-lumea/

Website Project: https://ivanpillow.github.io/L.U.M.E.A/?lang=en
